project: Des Moines AI Pulse — Web Platform Autonomy & Core Uplift
description: Deep uplift of the WEB platform across Security, Autonomy, Performance, UX, and Features. The governing theme: the site should run itself — content ingestion, data quality, moderation, publishing, marketing, and ops must not require manual admin touches; humans only handle escalated exceptions. Clusters in priority order: (1) WEB-SEC: close the publicly-callable/cost-abusable edge function holes and harden authz before adding more automation on top of them; (2) WEB-AUTO: build the autonomy control plane (job observability) then convert every manual admin queue (event submissions, data backfills, broken links, dedupe, stale content, articles, newsletters, moderation, creative approval, sitemaps, social, subscription lifecycle) into a self-running pipeline with AI scoring + human-exception escalation; (3) WEB-PERF: query payload + bundle + re-render fixes toward the <500KB / LCP<2.5s budgets; (4) WEB-UX: list-page state, loading/error consistency, a11y; (5) WEB-FEAT: web parity with shipped iOS monetization (contextual paywalls, annual+trial, ads/sponsored) plus engagement loops (saved searches+alerts, guest favorites, personalization). CONSTRAINTS THAT BIND EVERY STORY: follow CLAUDE.md backward-compatibility rules — live iOS/Android binaries call edge functions (get_active_ads, discover-chat, generate-itinerary, image-transform, validate-*-receipt, etc.), so NEVER tighten validation, rename/remove endpoints or fields, or lower rate limits below what shipped clients retry against in a single release; DB changes additive-only per the deprecation flow; console logs wrapped in import.meta.env.DEV; storage via @/lib/safeStorage; errors via @/lib/errorHandler. Ralph picks the highest-priority story with passes:false.

Per-user monthly quota checks for tiered AI features are enforced server-side (free/insider/vip limits matching useSubscription web copy), returning 429 with a structured body the web client surfaces as an upgrade prompt

BACKWARD COMPAT: limits are set at-or-above what shipped iOS binaries can legitimately hit (CLAUDE.md forbids tightening below what old clients retry against); response shapes for existing 200 paths unchanged

BACKWARD COMPAT: all limits kept at prior values (10/15min burst, 30/15min chat) so older iOS clients are unaffected; no 200-path response shapes changed. userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): scripts/audit-rls.ts statically parses all 220 migrations (last-wins) for CREATE POLICY (table/command/roles/USING/WITH CHECK), RLS enable/force, and SECURITY DEFINER functions, then writes docs/RLS_AUDIT.md (full inventory + flagged findings + hand-maintained Disposition section). REAL HOLE FIXED (migration 20260612000001): 8 policies named 'Service role can manage …' were actually FOR ALL USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) with NO role clause → defaulted to PUBLIC, letting any authenticated/anon caller read+write everyone's payments/invoices/subscriptions/usage/pseo rows (the permissive policy OR-ed away the per-user SELECT policies). Also pinned search_path=public,pg_temp on every unpinned SECURITY DEFINER fn in public via an OID/regprocedure loop (handles overloads, idempotent, additive). userStories.title: Automated brute-force login detection and temporary lockout
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need failed-login abuse handled automatically: the login_attempts table exists (migration 20260402000002) but nothing watches it, so credential-stuffing runs unimpeded.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth failure path records to login_attempts (ip, email, timestamp, success=false) via an edge function or existing hook — verify what already writes it and complete the wiring
A check at login time blocks (returns a 'try again later' state) when >5 failures from one IP or >10 for one email within 10 minutes; lockout expires automatically after 15 minutes
Lockout events are logged to security_audit_logs; the affected user gets a notification email (via existing Resend/SendGrid plumbing) on email-keyed lockouts
False-positive safety: successful login resets the counter; lockout never applies to a request presenting a valid existing session
Web login form surfaces the lockout state with a clear, non-enumerating message (same message whether or not the account exists)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): login_attempts truly had no consumer — check-login-attempt existed but was called by NOTHING in src/ (web used only a bypassable in-memory Map throttle in AuthContext). Wired the server-side function into AuthContext.login: pre-auth 'check' (blocks with the server message), 'record_failure' on auth error, 'record_success' on success (resets counter). New checkServerLockout() helper FAILS OPEN (returns null) on any error so an outage never blocks sign-in. Enhanced check-login-attempt: now locks on >10 failures for one EMAIL or >5 from one IP within a 10-min window (added IP-keyed counting via the existing client_ip column), lockout lasts 15 min; hardened IP extraction (CF-Connecting-IP, never the spoofable leftmost XFF); fail-open on DB error preserved. On the transition INTO lockout it writes a security_audit_logs row (event_type=account_lockout) and sends a best-effort notification email to the account owner via Resend + shared renderEmail — ONLY when a profile exists for the email (non-enumerating, no spam to random addresses; IP-only lockouts notify no one). Message is identical regardless of whether the account exists or which signal tripped (non-enumerating); Auth.tsx surfaces it via the existing toast. Valid-session requests never hit this path (login() is unauthenticated-only). Verified: type-check passes; edge fn parses via esbuild; AuthContext lints 0 errors. Evidence was: migration 20260402000002 + no caller.

userStories.title: Stop the Favorites undo flow from dropping queued backend deletes
userStories.description: As a user removing several favorites quickly, I need each removal to actually persist, because starting a new undo cancels the previous removal's commitTask without ever committing it — the item is gone from the local array but viewModel.remove*Favorite is never called for it, so it silently resurrects on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: Removing a second favorite while a prior undo is still pending flushes (commits) the prior removal to the backend instead of just cancelling its task
After multiple quick removals with no undo taps, all removed items are gone from the server on reload (optimistic UI matches server truth)

Implemented via a pending-removal queue or immediate commit-of-prior when a new removal starts (FavoritesView.swift:75/95/113)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. FavoritesView.swift removeEventWithUndo/removeRestaurantWithUndo/removeAttractionWithUndo (lines 75, 95, 113) call undoState?.commitTask?.cancel() before replacing undoState, but never await the prior remove* call. Data-integrity bug: the optimistically-removed item is dropped from the array yet never deleted on the backend. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added flushPendingRemoval() in FavoritesView; the three remove*WithUndo paths now flush (commit) the prior pending removal to the backend before starting a new undo instead of cancelling its commitTask uncommitted.

userStories.title: Implement Right Now ribbon counts or remove the count-driven copy

No dead count-formatting code left carrying a permanent 0

userStories.title: Surface Trip Planner load failures and roll back failed optimistic writes
userStories.description: As a Trip Planner user, I need errors to show and the UI to match the server, because itinerary fetch failures render as a blank itinerary, and optimistic reorder/delete operations swallow backend errors so the on-screen state silently diverges and reverts on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: ItineraryDetailView distinguishes 'fetch failed' from 'genuinely empty': fetchItems signals failure (throw/optional) and the view shows an error+retry state instead of a blank body when online with no items (TripPlannerService.swift:106 currently returns [] on RPC error)

Trip delete awaits the backend result before mutating savedTrips (or re-inserts + shows an error on failure) so deleted trips don't reappear unexplained (TripPlannerView.swift:311, TripPlannerService.swift:143)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ItineraryDetailView.swift:187 sets loadFailed only when items.isEmpty && !network.isConnected; an online RPC failure yields a blank itinerary. move()/persistOrder and deleteTrips mutate local state optimistically and swallow errors (DEBUG-only logging), so the visible order/list can permanently disagree with the server.

userStories.title: Gate pull-to-refresh haptics on actual success across remaining screens
userStories.description: As a user, I need pull-to-refresh to signal success only when the refresh succeeded, because Hotels, Weekend, and Articles fire UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally even when the view model set an errorMessage — the exact false-success anti-pattern fixed elsewhere under IOS-AUDIT-UX-005.
acceptanceCriteria: HotelsView, WeekendView, and ArticlesView branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil to play .success vs .error after refresh
DealsView's .refreshable closure gets success/error haptic feedback (currently none)
Behavior matches the already-fixed RestaurantsView/AttractionsView pattern
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. HotelsView.swift:76, WeekendView.swift:62, ArticlesView.swift:79 all call notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally while their VMs set errorMessage on failure (HotelsViewModel:82, WeekendViewModel:52, ArticlesViewModel:106). DealsView.swift:64 has no refresh haptic at all. | DONE (2026-06-24): HotelsView/ArticlesView/WeekendView refresh haptics now branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil ? .success : .error (canonical UX-005 pattern). DealsView .refreshable gained the same success/error haptic.

userStories.title: Show a stale-data error banner instead of a misleading empty state
userStories.description: As a user whose refresh fails while a filter is active, I need to see the real error, because Deals and Weekend hide a genuine load error behind a 'No Deals Found / clear filters' or featured-rails-only view when filtered/section data is empty but other data loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: DealsView surfaces the stale-data error banner when errorMessage != nil even if some allDeals exist but filteredDeals is empty, instead of showing 'No Deals Found' (DealsView.swift:25)

Genuine empty (no error) still shows the empty state; failures always offer retry
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DealsView.swift:25 only shows the error when allDeals.isEmpty. WeekendView.swift:29 gates errorBanner on 'errorMessage != nil && isEmpty' where isEmpty also requires featured rails empty — so an events-fetch failure with featured rails present hides the error and shows zero events with no explanation. | DONE (2026-06-24): WeekendView shows errorBanner inline when errorMessage != nil && populatedDays.isEmpty (events failed but featured rails loaded). userStories.title: Stop showing the password-reset success message inside a 'Sign In Error' alert
userStories.description: As a user requesting a password reset, I need a neutral success confirmation, because the success path routes its copy through setError(), which sets showError, fires an error haptic, and is rendered by an alert titled 'Sign In Error' — so a successful reset looks like a failure.
acceptanceCriteria: resetPassword() success uses a separate info/success channel (e.g. infoMessage) with a neutral alert title, not setError
No error haptic on the success path

userStories.title: Show a loading state during the search debounce instead of a blank screen

userStories.title: Make ScrollToTopButton robust to a missing 'scroll' coordinate space
userStories.description: As a developer using ScrollToTopButton, I need it to work without a hidden setup requirement, because its offset tracker reads frame(in: .named('scroll')) but the component never establishes that coordinate space — a caller who forgets it gets a button that silently never appears.
acceptanceCriteria: The component either bundles/sets the 'scroll' coordinate space itself (a wrapper that applies .coordinateSpace(.named('scroll'))) or loudly documents/asserts the requirement (ScrollToTopButton.swift:63)
With correct usage the button appears once the offset threshold is crossed; the silent-never-shows failure mode is eliminated
